evidence: The hunk shows `import { PADDING_RANGE } from "../src/themes/policy"` and the reviewer notes PADDING_WIDE is a literal 4; the agent dropped the import and gave a sound reason not to derive the constant from the range (range already pinned in session-globals.test.ts).
guidance_note: Run lint with warnings visible before pushing, so an unused import flagged only as a warn never reaches review.

evidence: The hunk shows mkdtempSync/mkdirSync run before the sun_path length guard, so a throw leaks both dirs; the agent moved the check ahead of any allocation (the reviewer's own second option) since mkdtempSync appends exactly six characters, which removes the leak rather than cleaning it up. The cited law is about branching on data vs control flow, not allocation order.
guidance_note: When adding a precondition guard to a function that allocates resources, put the guard before the first allocation.

evidence: The PR rewrote the section to give autoWrap/padding a session half while the unchanged line-741 sentence still said all four display-globals steppers have no SessionState half; the agent admitted the miss and narrowed the analogy to charset/colorCompatibility.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a documented fact, grep the whole doc for every other sentence stating the old fact (here "no SessionState half" / "four") before pushing.

evidence: Old code `chosen = sessionPick ?? configDefault ?? floor` then membership-checked only `chosen`, so a stale session pick went to the floor; the new effectiveGlobal path falls through to the config default. The agent confirmed by probe, kept the behaviour on purpose, and added discriminating tests (checked to fail against the old spelling). Keeping one precedence rule for every field is a fair use of one-source-of-truth.
guidance_note: When a refactor routes old functions through a shared helper, list every case where old and new outputs differ, and either pin each with a test or state the change in the PR body before review.

evidence: Same precedence change as F4, plus the stale presets.ts comment ("collapse to the floor, visibly"), which the agent rewrote to describe the precedence chain. The agent's side correction (charset/colorCompatibility are not session-targeted in this PR) is accurate according to the F3 doc text.
guidance_note: When a behaviour change is intended, grep for comments describing the old behaviour ("collapse to the floor") across the repo in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer was right that `wrapEverywhere` was declared but never rendered, so the snippet did not show the pair its prose claimed. It was wrong that `sessionPadding` was vestigial: the agent found it seeds an unset `set: padding` stepper, kept it, and corrected its comment.
guidance_note: For a doc snippet that claims to demonstrate a pattern, check that every declared action is referenced by the template, since the CI check:pass only proves the snippet loads.

evidence: Every row of the autoWrap it.each passed `configured = true`, which equals DEFAULT_WRAP and any mis-parse to true, so the table could not fail. The agent switched to `configured = false` and added a converse guard ("true"/"false" beat a disagreeing default).
guidance_note: When writing a fall-through test, choose an expected value that differs from both the floor and every wrong outcome, so the test can tell the correct path apart from a coincidence.

evidence: The hunk shows the old `chosen = sessionStyle ?? globalsStyle ?? "powerline"; isStripStyle(chosen) ? chosen : "powerline"` replaced by effectiveGlobal, while the retained comment still says a stale entry "collapses to the floor". The agent fixed both comments and added `effectiveStripStyle("no-such-style", "capsule") === "capsule"`.
guidance_note: When rewriting a function body, re-read its header comment against the new code; this one was edited in the same hunk and still described the old rule.

narrative: There was one review round with eight advisories, all real: a dead import, a temp-dir leak on a guard's throw path, two doc/comment drifts, a vacuous autoWrap test table, and an unannounced precedence change (stale session pick now falls to the config default rather than the floor) reported three times (F4, F5, F8). The agent kept the precedence change on purpose, pinned it with tests it confirmed fail against the old code, and fixed the stale comments. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The precedence widening was an intended behaviour change shipped as a refactor side effect with no test and stale comments; stating it in the PR body with a pinning test would have removed three findings.
The agent checked each pushback-adjacent claim by direct probe (e.g. `effectiveStripStyle("muted", "capsule")`) before accepting, which kept the replies accurate.

evidence: dispatch runs every effect even after one fails, so the realize dual arm's `[persist-effect, clear-state]` pair could wipe the session pick after a rejected write. The agent made the release a trailing segment on set-config/step-config, cleared only after writeConfigOverride, and deleted clear-state (b6c8be1 diff). That is the reviewer's "run only after the write succeeds" option.
guidance_note: Before relying on two effects in one click being atomic, read dispatch's failure semantics; a destructive effect that depends on another succeeding belongs in the same handler.

evidence: The hand-maintained NUMERIC_GLOBALS_FLOORS meant a new numeric field could silently seed from min. Rather than restore the generic scan (which was what missed the floor), the agent typed the table as Record<NumericGlobalsField, number> so a missing floor is a compile error. That is sound in intent, but the type direction it shipped was wrong (see F21).
guidance_note: When introducing a hand-maintained table keyed by a type's fields, make it total over a derived key type in the original PR rather than relying on contributors to remember it.

evidence: The loop asserted each URL clears "theme" OR "padding", so swapped targets would pass; b6c8be1 replaces it with two assertions pinned to `set-config ... args[3] === "theme"` and `step-config ... args[3] === "padding"`.
guidance_note: When one assertion loops over several subjects, pin each subject to its own expected value; an OR across subjects cannot detect swaps.

evidence: The diagram showed ↺ only after wrap/padding while declareSettingControls gives every picker a reset and the next paragraph says so; b6c8be1's docs diff adds ↺ after all controls.
guidance_note: Generate or check doc diagrams against a real render of the bar rather than drawing them by hand.

evidence: This duplicates F3 on the same OR loop and was fixed by the same b6c8be1 edit splitting the assertion per key.
guidance_note: When one assertion loops over several subjects, pin each subject to its own expected value; an OR across subjects cannot detect swaps.

evidence: OTHER_SID's menu was closed, so the theme name could not appear in its render whether or not isolation worked; b6c8be1 opens the other session's menu first and also asserts it shows its own "🎨 tokyo-night", which makes the absence meaningful.
guidance_note: For every not.toContain assertion, first assert the same render can show the value (here the session's own default), so the negative check has something to compare against.

evidence: The hunk shows `return null` on the first missing key despite a comment promising every failure is reported; b6c8be1 switches to `ok = false; continue` and returns after the loop.
guidance_note: When a comment promises all failures are reported, make sure the loop body never returns early.

evidence: After styleControl was deleted, nothing read `activeStyle: { kind: "state", key: "style" }`; b6c8be1 deletes it and its comment block. The fix did not sweep the other residue of the same deletion (see F12).
guidance_note: When deleting a segment, grep the file for every name it introduced or referenced (vars, actions, comment mentions) and remove the residue in the same commit.

evidence: jest.setTimeout applies to the whole file, but the comment claimed only the heap-snapshot block was affected; b6c8be1 moves it to file scope with a comment naming the effect on the concurrency gate.
guidance_note: Check the documented scope of a framework call (jest.setTimeout is file-scoped) before writing a comment that claims a narrower scope.

evidence: b6c8be1 (F1's fix) introduced releaseSessionKey with a new throw path after writeConfigOverride, and its tests covered only the happy-path release. The agent added a test that drives set-config with an unregistered release key and asserts both the throw and the on-disk write (e199b3c).
guidance_note: When a fix exists to guarantee an ordering, ship a test in the same commit that drives the failing side and asserts the ordering held.

evidence: Flag false positive: b6c8be1 does not touch compileDual or CONFIG_KEY_TO_EFFECTIVE_VAR (its action.ts change is only the realize release mapping), so the missing `preset` entry comes from the original PR making preset a dual control. The agent added `["preset", "preset.effective"]` in e199b3c.
guidance_note: When new code reads through a lookup map with a silent fallback, check that every key the new callers pass has an entry; here that means the preset dual control.

evidence: The stale comments naming themeControl/lookControl/wrapToggleControl/paddingControl come from the original deletion, not from b6c8be1. They are the same class of residue F8 flagged (activeStyle orphaned by deleting styleControl), and F8's fix removed only the one variable without sweeping the file for other references to the deleted segments. e199b3c fixed this block plus four more references.
guidance_note: When fixing one orphan left by a deletion, grep for every name the deleted code introduced and remove all residue in the same commit.

evidence: b6c8be1 deleted VERB_CLEAR_STATE and moved the release onto set-config/step-config, but CLAUDE.md still described "a `clear-state` on the session key, in one atomic dispatch". The agent called it self-inflicted and rewrote the paragraph in e199b3c.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes a named construct (a verb, a function), grep the repo for its name, including CLAUDE.md and docs, before pushing.

evidence: b6c8be1 rewrote the realize dual-arm code to `effects.map(... args: [...e.args, c.sessionKey])` but left the comment above it saying "a second effect in the same atomic dispatch ... what clear-state writes"; e199b3c rewrites it.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites code, re-read the comment block directly above the edited lines in the same commit.

evidence: Flag false positive: the missing persistWhen cross-ref check is original-PR surface (actions.ts DISCRIMINATOR_KEYS), not a change b6c8be1 made. A typo'd selector loading cleanly and silently staying session-only is a real silent failure. The fix checked only global variables, which caused F20.
guidance_note: When adding a field that is read back as a reference, add the load-time resolution check over every scope the runtime resolves it through (here render.ts's stateKeyToVar, global and segment vars).

evidence: Flag false positive: b6c8be1 does not touch test/helpers/ambient-chrome.ts. The first-match writtenKey chain predates duals and drops the persist half of a DualActionDecl. Dormant, but a real trap; e199b3c folds it through actionDestinations.
guidance_note: When widening a union so one value can carry two previously exclusive keys, grep for if/else-if chains over those keys and convert them in the same PR.

evidence: b6c8be1's policy.ts diff removes `export const NUMERIC_GLOBALS_FLOORS` but keeps its preceding comment block, leaving it orphaned above parseSessionBoolean; the agent: "I moved the table and left its comment behind."
guidance_note: When moving a declaration to another file, move or delete its comment block in the same hunk.

evidence: Flag false positive: SETTINGS_WRITTEN_KEYS's hand-typed "autoWrap"/"padding" are original-PR code that b6c8be1 did not touch. They contradicted the comment's "derived from the same records" claim, and e199b3c introduces WRAP/PADDING records.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a set is derived from records, check that no entry is a literal; if one is, make it a record before writing the claim.

evidence: Flag false positive: e199b3c does not touch the padding-stepper test; it is original-PR code asserting only toContain at each state, unlike the theme tests that assert exclusivity. 8b5acc6 adds the not.toContain checks for both states.
guidance_note: When testing a destination switch, assert both that the new destination is present and that the old one is absent, for every affordance kind and not only the first one written.

evidence: e199b3c's new check scanned only `Object.values(cfg.variables)`, but stateKeyToVar (which resolves the selector at render) and hasStateKind in the same file also cover segment `vars`, so configs that previously loaded and worked were rejected. 8b5acc6 factors a shared stateVars helper over both scopes and adds a test.
guidance_note: When adding a load-time check that a reference resolves, read the runtime resolver it mirrors and any sibling helper in the same file (hasStateKind) and use the same scope set.

evidence: F2's fix (b6c8be1 globals.ts diff) introduced `number extends NonNullable<Globals[K]>`, which drops a literal-union numeric field like `1 | 2 | 3`, so the promised compile error does not hold for that shape. 8b5acc6 flips it to `NonNullable<Globals[K]> extends number`.
guidance_note: When a type exists to force a compile error, check it against a deliberately non-compliant probe of each plausible field shape (plain number, literal union) before claiming the guarantee.

evidence: The orphaned "toggle's members and the stepper's bounds" comment is residue of moving wrap/padding into settings-menu.ts. F12's fix (e199b3c) swept five references to deleted controls in default-dsl-config.ts but missed this one, and the agent also found a remaining "four .3 steppers" count.
guidance_note: When sweeping residue of moved code, grep for the concepts (toggle, stepper, four) as well as the deleted identifiers.

narrative: Round 0 found nine real problems, chiefly a split-able two-effect durable write (F1), which the agent fixed well by folding the release into the write handler. That fix and F2's typed-floor fix produced five round-1/round-2 findings: two stale descriptions of the deleted clear-state verb, an orphaned comment, a missing failure-path test, and a backwards conditional type. The F15 cross-ref check rejected valid segment-local selectors (F20), and incomplete comment sweeps after deleting segments ran from F8 through F12 to F22. Rounds 1 and 2 also carried original-PR findings (F11, F15, F16, F18, F19), so only round 3 is fully avoidable.
guidance_observations: Every reply accepted, and every premise checked out; the cost came from fixes that were right in design but not swept for residue (comments, CLAUDE.md, moved declarations).

Fixes that delete or move a named construct (clear-state, NUMERIC_GLOBALS_FLOORS, the old controls) were each followed by a stale-reference finding; a repo-wide grep for the removed name per fix would have prevented F13, F14, F17, F12 and F22.
New load-time checks and new type guards were shipped without probing them against the runtime resolver or a non-compliant input, causing F20 and F21.

evidence: menuPageKey(stateKey) = stateKey + ".page" starts with MENU_NS, so the prefix filter admits page-nav writes (latent). Instead of hardcoding `.endsWith(".page")`, the agent matched the opener's exact structure `e.args[3] === menuPageKey(e.args[1])`, which keeps the suffix single-sourced and drops the prefix test.
guidance_note: When writing a test helper that classifies effects, match the exact shape the producer emits rather than a key prefix shared by other producers.

evidence: CLAUDE.md cited edit chrome as the static "+" example while edit-chrome.ts binds "+"/"✕" and says it is deliberately not static; the agent admitted writing the line before changing edit chrome and removed the instance claim in e75bdfc.
guidance_note: After changing a design mid-PR (edit chrome moving from static to a per-state pair), grep the PR's own prose for claims about the earlier design.

evidence: analyzeMenuCall permits non-literal displays, so parseMenuArgs's `display #N is not text` throw was the only gate and had no test. The agent added one using a shape that still loads after the F7 fix, and found it renders as an on-bar diagnostic rather than throwing.
guidance_note: Every new throw message gets a test that triggers it, in the PR that adds it.

evidence: This duplicates F2 on the same CLAUDE.md line, also noting the conflict with docs/interaction-authoring.md:611's `{{ menu "addAfterGit" "+" "✕" }}`; it was fixed by the same e75bdfc edit.
guidance_note: After changing a design mid-PR, grep the PR's own prose for claims about the earlier design.

evidence: The file's CANONICAL catalog still showed `{{ menu "apply" [(dict …)] }}`, which cycleDisplayIssue now rejects with "needs a display". The agent updated it and swept examples/, finding nothing else.
guidance_note: When a grammar change makes a spelling illegal, grep every example and doc file for that spelling, not only the instances next to edited lines.

evidence: legacy-parity.json5's template was migrated but its comment still said "the apply name is the whole declaration", while showcase.json5 was updated in the same PR; the agent aligned the wording.
guidance_note: When a migration updates a comment in one file, grep for the same sentence in the other files and update every copy.

evidence: The loader's syntactic isDictCall and the renderer's structural isDict disagree for `(merge (dict …))`. The agent noted the renderer only sees values and that limiting to literal dicts would forbid dynamic displays, then rejected only the ambiguous window (unclassifiable last expr where the options-reading also yields a legal display count) and tested every reachable shape.
guidance_note: When the same input is classified at load and again at render, write down the shape table for both predicates in the original PR and reject every row where they can disagree.

evidence: The test name claims "themePage" renders on the bar, but the body only asserted `load(...)).not.toThrow()`. The agent added `buildRuntime(...).render()` containing "themePage" via a shared srcFor fixture.
guidance_note: Make each test body assert the behaviour its name claims; a render claim needs a render assertion.

evidence: Same root cause as F7, with the worse case that an object holding only closeOnPick/paged/key is silently accepted as options. Fixed by the same loader rejection. The agent declined the "compare against loader-declared count" variant because there is no loader-to-render channel, a claim consistent with the renderer receiving only evaluated template args.
guidance_note: When the same input is classified at load and again at render, write down the shape table for both predicates in the original PR and reject every row where they can disagree.

narrative: One review round raised nine real advisories: stale docs and examples after the grammar change (F2, F4, F5, F6), test gaps (F1, F3, F8), and a load-vs-render classification mismatch for the trailing options dict (F7, F9). The agent took different fixes where the suggested cure was a literal or too blunt, and those fixes held: round 1 found nothing. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: Four of nine findings were stale prose or examples after a grammar change; one grep for the old `{{ menu "x" }}` spelling and for sentences describing the old model would have caught them before review.
The agent's different-fix replies listed every reachable shape and the tests that discovered plan corrections (the boolean-literal case), which is why the fixes produced no follow-up findings.
